The game separates the two landmasses, but the mainland shape is the primary visual cue for this puzzle.

The percentage and arrow hints are more valuable than the distance number. On this board, a guess of 50% distance might still leave you 1,000 km away, but the arrow tells you exactly which way to pivot. For Malaysia, the arrow often points sharply south or southeast. If you guess a country in India, the arrow will point almost directly east. Use these directional shifts to triangulate the position. The game doesn't lie about the bearing. A consistent eastward arrow from a western starting point means you are looking at a country on the other side of the Indian Ocean or the South China Sea.

Remember that the game calculates distance from the center of your guessed country to the center of the target. A guess of a long, thin country like Chile or Norway can skew your perception of the target's location. Always account for the size of your guess. If you are off by 10 degrees in direction, you might still be in the right ocean but on the wrong continent. Check the daily hints page if the arrow logic gets confusing.

Mistakes that waste guesses

The most common error is guessing Indonesia. While it shares the same latitude and is a neighbor, Indonesia is an archipelago. Its silhouette looks nothing like the solid mainland shape of Malaysia. Players often confuse the two because they are both tropical and share the Malay language family. This mistake burns a guess and sends you on a tangent toward the islands of the Pacific.

Another frequent slip-up is guessing Thailand. Thailand sits directly north of Malaysia and shares a similar vertical orientation. However, Thailand has a much wider northern section and a distinct "head" shape that Malaysia lacks. If your arrow points south after guessing Thailand, you are likely close, but the shape mismatch is the real clue. Don't assume similarity in border length means similarity in shape.

The distance metric is a straight line from the geographic center of your guess to the center of the target. If you guess a country that is far away, the distance is large.
